sentinel: this file marks the materialised data dir for the ML01 topic
title: Dropout regularization strategies on shallow tabular MLPs
research_question: Does the choice of dropout variant (standard / spatial / variational) matter more for probability calibration than for test accuracy on tabular classification with shallow MLPs?

hypotheses.statement: Variational / MC dropout produces lower ECE than standard element-wise dropout on at least 2 of 3 tabular classification benchmarks, averaged over >=5 seeds.
Test-set accuracy differs by <2 absolute percentage points between dropout variants on datasets where all methods exceed 95% accuracy.
The no-dropout control is strictly worse than at least one dropout variant in ECE on at least 2 of 3 datasets.

note: Single-topic L1 slice of the 55-topic ARC-Bench. In the original bench a research framework (AIDE / rc_full / rc_copilot / AI-Scientist-v2 / AgentLab) executes real code over >=5 seeds and is rubric-judged. Here the 'research agent' is the tmeoa LLM gateway (qwen3.6-35b-a3b): it is prompted with the manifest and must produce a structured result (per-condition metric numbers + per-hypothesis verdicts + writeup). The runner computes a real rubric_weighted_score proxy from that output (metric coverage x condition coverage x hypothesis coverage x plausibility), NOT the full manual rubric. See port_notes in result.json.
